minecraft_courtyard_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: before/after example for an open-source photo editing Skill.
Input image: the supplied courtyard photo is the edit target. Transform that exact scene, not a different village.
Primary request: rebuild every visible surface and object as a believable screenshot inside Minecraft Java Edition using the classic default resource-pack look and vanilla Fancy lighting, no shaders or Vibrant Visuals. It must read as Minecraft in-game geometry and materials, not generic cute voxels, LEGO or pixelated photography.
Keep: landscape 3:2 crop, eye-level camera, back wall, four-pane window left of the centered green door, bench at left, one red bicycle at right, small plants and paving, their relative positions and scale. Keep the shot recognizably the same courtyard.
Geometry/material mapping: walls as coarse pale stone block faces with restrained low-resolution square pixel textures; square tiled stone paving and stair slab at doorway; bench built from oak stairs/slabs; foliage as cubic leaf clusters with flat pixel-cutout plants; cuboid pipe and simple square glass panes. The door is a dark green block-built equivalent in the same position. Bicycle is a small red block-built prop approximated with stepped octagonal wheels and thin red cuboid frame, keep both wheels and its overall bicycle silhouette. Do not replace it with a different vehicle.
Rendering: coherent one-block world grid, larger flat cuboid surfaces, clearly nearest-neighbor low-resolution texels within each block face rather than millions of tiny cubes. Vanilla face-dependent shading and modest corner ambient occlusion, overcast diffuse daylight; no cinematic haze, glossy ray tracing, bloom, deep depth-of-field or rounded bevels.
Avoid: unchanged photographic plaster or moss, blurred textures, smooth realistic wheels, toy miniatures, isometric viewpoint, UI, crosshair, HUD, labels, logos or watermark.
